detail.longDescription: I am trying to connect my self-managed K8s cluster to my GitLab using agentk GitLab for Kubernetes. When I run the command provided by the GitLab which contains the generated token and the GitLab certificate file using Helm, the GitLab UI shows it was connected but goes down directly. I checked logs for GitLab agents's pods but nothing seems problematic. kubectl logs -n test -l app.kubernetes.io/name=gitlab-agent --prefix | grep -Ei 'kas|tunnel|registrar|error|warn|failed|grpc|unauth|token|connect' [pod/test-gitlab-agent-v2-77b4cf557b-5rls2/gitlab-agent] {"time":"2026-09-01T06:54:08.995033283Z","level":"INFO","msg":"Starting","mod_name":"agent2kas_tunnel"} [pod/test-gitlab-agent-v2-77b4cf557b-5rls2/gitlab-agent] {"time":"2026-09-01T06:54:08.99532843Z","level":"INFO","msg":"Starting","mod_name":"agent_registrar"} [pod/test-gitlab-agent-v2-77b4cf557b-9jqqm/gitlab-agent] {"time":"2026-09-01T06:54:18.712666094Z","level":"INFO","msg":"Starting","mod_name":"agent_registrar"} [pod/test-gitlab-agent-v2-77b4cf557b-9jqqm/gitlab-agent] {"time":"2026-09-01T06:54:18.712666026Z","level":"INFO","msg":"Starting","mod_name":"agent2kas_tunnel"} The KAS is also reached from the cluster. Does anyone have any idea why GitLab cannot have a stable connection on the Kubernetes cluster?
